# Read-Back

A three-course dinner for six people must be ready and served by 19:30 (7:30 PM). One cook manages two burners and one oven. The meal consists of a leek-and-potato soup starter, braised short ribs main course, and an apple tart dessert. Mise en place (chopping mirepoix, trimming ribs, measuring stock) takes 40 minutes and happens first. The oven heats for 20 minutes, then braises the ribs for 3 hours starting after searing and building the braising liquid (total ~3.5 hours oven time). While the ribs braise, the soup is started two hours in (sweat leeks 10 min, simmer potatoes 30 min, blend 5 min, then held warm on the back burner). After the ribs rest for 20 minutes, the braising liquid is reduced for 15 minutes. The tart shell is rolled and chilled for 30–120 minutes, then apples are arranged (20 min), and it bakes for 45 minutes starting the moment the ribs leave the oven. Service is sequential: soup is plated and served (10 min at table), then main plates are plated (5 min work) and served after 10 minutes of guests eating soup; dessert is sliced and served 20 minutes after main plates are cleared (10 min service). The cook is the sole constraint on parallelization; the oven and burners are also exclusive resources.
